=== let with and without a type
tariff "t"
let a = 1
let b: Money = $5
---
tariff "t"
let a = 1
let b: Money = $5

=== var and assignments
tariff "t"
var total = $0
total = $1
total += $2
total -= $3
---
tariff "t"
var total = $0
total = $1
total += $2
total -= $3

=== charge with options only
tariff "t"
charge "Linehaul" (quantity: miles, rate: rate)
---
tariff "t"
charge (text "Linehaul") (quantity:miles rate:rate)

=== charge with a code and an amount
tariff "t"
charge "Fuel surcharge" as FSC = linehaul * fuelPercent
---
tariff "t"
charge (text "Fuel surcharge") as FSC = (* linehaul fuelPercent)

=== charge with a code, options and an amount
tariff "t"
charge "Detention" as DET (quantity: billable, rate: $65/h) = owed
---
tariff "t"
charge (text "Detention") as DET (quantity:billable rate:$65/[h]) = owed

=== charge with an interpolated label
tariff "t"
charge "Detention, stop {stop.sequence}" as DET = owed
---
tariff "t"
charge (text "Detention, stop " (. stop sequence)) as DET = owed

=== charge called as a function is an expression
tariff "t"
charge(XDROP)
---
tariff "t"
expr (call charge XDROP)

=== note
tariff "t"
note "Priced from the {lane.origin.city} tariff"
---
tariff "t"
note (text "Priced from the " (. (. lane origin) city) " tariff")

=== if statement
tariff "t"
if drops > 1 {
  charge "Extra drops" = $75
}
---
tariff "t"
if (> drops 1)
  charge (text "Extra drops") = $75

=== if else if else
tariff "t"
if a {
  note "a"
} else if b {
  note "b"
} else {
  note "c"
}
---
tariff "t"
if a
  note (text "a")
else if b
  note (text "b")
else
  note (text "c")

=== else on the next line
tariff "t"
if a {
  note "a"
}
else {
  note "b"
}
---
tariff "t"
if a
  note (text "a")
else
  note (text "b")

=== if let
tariff "t"
if let w = shipment.weight {
  note "{w}"
} else {
  fail "No weight"
}
---
tariff "t"
if let w = (. shipment weight)
  note (text w)
else
  fail (text "No weight")

=== single line if
tariff "t"
if shipment.hazmat { charge "Hazmat" as HAZ = $50 }
---
tariff "t"
if (. shipment hazmat)
  charge (text "Hazmat") as HAZ = $50

=== match statement with block arms
tariff "t"
match shipment.serviceType.code {
  "EXP" => {
    charge "Expedite" as EXP = $100
  }
  _ => {
    note "Standard"
  }
}
---
tariff "t"
match (. (. shipment serviceType) code)
  arm (text "EXP") =>
    charge (text "Expedite") as EXP = $100
  arm _ =>
    note (text "Standard")

=== match statement with expression arms
tariff "t"
match stop.kind {
  Pickup => note "pickup"
  Delivery => note "delivery"
  _ => detention(stop.dwell ?? 0 h, rate: $65/h)
}
---
tariff "t"
match (. stop kind)
  arm Pickup =>
    note (text "pickup")
  arm Delivery =>
    note (text "delivery")
  arm _ => (call detention (?? (. stop dwell) 0[h]) rate:$65/[h])

=== match arm with a guard
tariff "t"
match pieces {
  n if n > 10 => {
    charge "Bulk" = $10
  }
  _ => {}
}
---
tariff "t"
match pieces
  arm (bind n) if (> n 10) =>
    charge (text "Bulk") = $10
  arm _ =>

=== match statement arm with a guard that ends in a name
tariff "t"
match pieces {
  n if bulk => {
    charge "Bulk" = $10
  }
  _ => {}
}
---
tariff "t"
match pieces
  arm (bind n) if bulk =>
    charge (text "Bulk") = $10
  arm _ =>

=== for loop
tariff "t"
for stop in shipment.stops {
  note "{stop.sequence}"
}
---
tariff "t"
for stop in (. shipment stops)
  note (text (. stop sequence))

=== for loop with a filter
tariff "t"
for stop in shipment.stops where stop.dwell != none {
  continue
}
---
tariff "t"
for stop in (. shipment stops) where (!= (. stop dwell) none)
  continue

=== for over a range
tariff "t"
for i in 0..3 {
  break
}
---
tariff "t"
for i in (.. 0 3)
  break

=== require
tariff "t"
require shipment.distance > 0 mi else "This rate needs a distance"
---
tariff "t"
require (> (. shipment distance) 0[mi]) else (text "This rate needs a distance")

=== require let
tariff "t"
require let w = shipment.weight else "This rate needs the shipment's weight"
---
tariff "t"
require let w = (. shipment weight) else (text "This rate needs the shipment's weight")

=== fail statement
tariff "t"
fail "No rate for {lane.origin.zip3}"
---
tariff "t"
fail (text "No rate for " (. (. lane origin) zip3))

=== return in a function
library "l"
fn f() -> Int {
  return 1
}
---
library "l"
fn f() -> Int
  return 1

=== return at file level is parsed
tariff "t"
return 1
---
tariff "t"
return 1

=== total clauses
tariff "t"
minimum $450
maximum $5_000
round to cents
---
tariff "t"
minimum $450
maximum $5000
round half-up to cents

=== round modes
tariff "t"
round half even to cents
round up to $5
round down to $1
---
tariff "t"
round half-even to cents
round up to $5
round down to $1

=== round to a constant
tariff "t"
round to INCREMENT
---
tariff "t"
round half-up to INCREMENT

=== given and expect
tariff "t"
test "t" {
  given shipment.weight = 1_240 lb
  given input.rate = $2.10/mi
  given shipment.stops = [pickup(arrival: @2026-01-05T08:00Z), delivery()]
  expect charge("Linehaul") == $365.30
  expect lines.len == 2
}
---
tariff "t"
test "t"
  given shipment.weight = 1240[lb]
  given input.rate = $2.10/[mi]
  given shipment.stops = (list (call pickup arrival:@2026-01-05T08:00:00+0m) (call delivery))
  expect (== (call charge (text "Linehaul")) $365.30)
  expect (== (. lines len) 2)

=== expect fails
tariff "t"
test "t" {
  expect fails
  expect fails "This rate needs the shipment's weight"
}
---
tariff "t"
test "t"
  expect fails
  expect fails (text "This rate needs the shipment's weight")

=== expression statement
tariff "t"
deficit(breaks, actual: w)
---
tariff "t"
expr (call deficit breaks actual:w)

=== statements inside a function body
library "l"
fn total(xs: List<Money>) -> Money {
  var sum = $0
  for x in xs {
    sum += x
  }
  return sum
}
---
library "l"
fn total(xs: List<Money>) -> Money
  var sum = $0
  for x in xs
    sum += x
  return sum

=== continuation after an operator
tariff "t"
let a = 1 +
  2
---
tariff "t"
let a = (+ 1 2)

=== continuation before an operator
tariff "t"
let a = linehaul
  + fuel
  - discount
---
tariff "t"
let a = (- (+ linehaul fuel) discount)

=== continuation before a method chain
tariff "t"
let a = shipment.stops
  .where(s => s.kind == Delivery)
  ?.first
---
tariff "t"
let a = (?. (call (. (. shipment stops) where) (lambda (s) (== (. s kind) Delivery))) first)

=== continuation before a coalesce and logic
tariff "t"
let a = x
  ?? y
let b = p
  and q
  or r
---
tariff "t"
let a = (?? x y)
let b = (or (and p q) r)

=== a new line before a call does not continue
tariff "t"
let a = f
(1)
---
tariff "t"
let a = f
expr (paren 1)

=== a new line before an index does not continue
tariff "t"
let a = xs
[1]
---
tariff "t"
let a = xs
expr (list 1)

=== value on the line after equals
tariff "t"
let a =
  5
---
tariff "t"
let a = 5

=== arrow continues to the next line
tariff "t"
let a = match x {
  A =>
    1
  _ => 2
}
---
tariff "t"
let a = (match x [A => 1] [_ => 2])

=== best with options
tariff "t"
best "Linehaul" {
  option "Per mile" {
    charge "Linehaul" (quantity: shipment.distance, rate: rate)
  }
  option "Flat" {
    charge "Flat rate" = flatRate
  }
}
---
tariff "t"
best "Linehaul"
  option "Per mile"
    charge (text "Linehaul") (quantity:(. shipment distance) rate:rate)
  option "Flat"
    charge (text "Flat rate") = flatRate

=== worst inside an if
tariff "t"
if shipment.hazmat {
  worst "Floor" {
    option "A" {
      charge "A" = $1
    }
    option "B" {
      charge "B" = $2
    }
  }
}
---
tariff "t"
if (. shipment hazmat)
  worst "Floor"
    option "A"
      charge (text "A") = $1
    option "B"
      charge (text "B") = $2

=== a choice holds only options
tariff "t"
best "x" {
  charge "A" = $1
}
---
tariff "t"
best "x"
! syntax 24..30 A choice holds only `option "Label"` blocks, one for each method

=== an option outside a choice
tariff "t"
option "A" {
  charge "A" = $1
}
---
tariff "t"
best ""
  option "A"
    charge (text "A") = $1
! misplaced 11..17 An `option` can only be written inside `best` or `worst`

=== best, worst and option are names elsewhere
tariff "t"
let best = 1
let option = best + 2
let worst = [option]
---
tariff "t"
let best = 1
let option = (+ best 2)
let worst = (list option)

=== vary and assume outside a property
tariff "t"
test "t" {
  vary shipment.weight in 1 lb..2 lb
  assume true
}
---
tariff "t"
test "t"
  vary shipment.weight in (.. 1[lb] 2[lb])
  assume true
! misplaced 24..28 `vary` can only be used inside a `property` block
! misplaced 61..67 `assume` can only be used inside a `property` block

=== assume reads a charge call
tariff "t"
property "p" {
  vary shipment.weight in 1 lb..2 lb
  assume charge("Linehaul") != none
  expect true
}
---
tariff "t"
property "p"
  vary shipment.weight in (.. 1[lb] 2[lb])
  assume (!= (call charge (text "Linehaul")) none)
  expect true

=== assume with a space before a parenthesis is the statement
tariff "t"
fn assume(x: Bool) -> Bool = x
property "p" {
  vary shipment.weight in 1 lb..2 lb
  assume (shipment.weight ?? 0 lb) > 1 lb
  let ok = assume(true)
  expect ok
}
---
tariff "t"
fn assume(x: Bool) -> Bool = x
property "p"
  vary shipment.weight in (.. 1[lb] 2[lb])
  assume (> (paren (?? (. shipment weight) 0[lb])) 1[lb])
  let ok = (call assume true)
  expect ok

=== a property expects no refusal
tariff "t"
property "p" {
  vary shipment.weight in 1 lb..2 lb
  expect fails
}
---
tariff "t"
property "p"
  vary shipment.weight in (.. 1[lb] 2[lb])
  expect fails
! misplaced 72..77 A property can't expect a refusal: it states what holds when the tariff rates. Narrow it with `assume` or its ranges instead

=== monotone expect outside a property
tariff "t"
test "t" {
  expect total nondecreasing in shipment.weight
}
---
tariff "t"
test "t"
  expect total nondecreasing in shipment.weight
! misplaced 37..50 `nondecreasing` can only be used inside a `property` block
